# costgraph_kubernetes_cluster (Resource)

Reserve a Kubernetes cluster name in a CostGraph tenant before installing the operator. This resource does not create a Kubernetes cluster, deploy the operator, issue credentials, or report collection health. The operator reports versions, inventory, and heartbeats separately and adopts the reserved registration when its cluster name and tenant match.

Requires an organization owner's user API key explicitly granted organization:manage and a deployment with the Kubernetes registration management API. Keep the operator's tenant-bound collection credential in an existing Kubernetes Secret.

Import an existing active registration by its cluster UUID. An active name in the same tenant cannot be created twice. Changing the name or tenant replaces the registration. Destroying it disconnects collection and retains historical records. Remove the operator first, or reference this resource from its Helm release so Terraform orders removal. A collector cannot recreate a disconnected name until an owner explicitly reserves it again, which creates a new UUID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "costgraph" {}

variable "tenant_id" {
  description = "Tenant UUID associated with the operator's collection credential."
  type        = string
}

resource "costgraph_kubernetes_cluster" "production" {
  name      = "production-aks"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Cluster name, matching global.clusterName in the operator Helm chart. It must not be blank or have surrounding whitespace. Changing it replaces the registration.
- `tenant_id` (String) Lowercase UUID of the tenant that owns the collector credential. Changing it replaces the registration.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Cluster registration UUID used for management and import.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization UUID associated with the management API key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import costgraph_kubernetes_cluster.production 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
```
